components.name: Shell Primary Button

components.name: Drill Primary Button
components.description: Ink-on-white pill, the drill zone's primary action. 44px touch target.
components.css: .ds-btn-drill { background: #1d1d1f; color: #ffffff; padding: 0 24px; min-height: 44px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; transition: background 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 0.18s; } .ds-btn-drill:hover { background: #000000; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-drill:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(29,29,31,0.35); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-drill:disabled { opacity: 0.66; transform: none; }

components.name: Shell Card

components.css: .ds-card-shell { background: #121212; color: #fafafa; border: 1px solid #262626; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 20px; box-shadow: 0 2px 12px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5); font-family: 'Outfit', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-shell h3 { margin: 0 0 6px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 650; } .ds-card-shell p { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; color: #a3a3a3; line-height: 1.6; }

narrative.northStar: The Coach's Workspace, in Four Rooms
narrative.overview: LSAT U is one app that currently speaks in four related visual dialects: a disciplined dark-first graphite chassis built on HSL tokens with a bronze ember accent, plus three lighter rooms (the graphite near-monochrome drill zone, the warm paper-and-ink inbox, and the Apple-slate mainhub island). Bootcamps run fully scoped worlds behind wrapper classes. The through-line is restraint and truthfulness: color carries meaning, never identity; motion conveys state, never theatre. The honest tension, recorded rather than hidden: the rooms do not yet share one token vocabulary, so a future convergence can be deliberate.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first shell, light task rooms; depth via near-black layering and soft shadow, not glow.
Color is semantic, not brand. The only brand color is a bronze ember used sparingly.
One accent rule per room; no room runs a saturated identity color across its surface.
Scoped CSS-variable systems keep bootcamp worlds out of the chassis.
Attempt-state colors are named apart from system-status colors so a self-report never reads as a judgment.

rules.name: The Meaning-Not-Identity Rule
rules.body: Chromatic color appears only to signal state. No room uses a saturated color as identity; the bronze ember stays under 10% of any surface.

rules.name: The Self-Report Firewall Rule
rules.body: state-again and state-easy are aliased to wrong/correct hues but kept under distinct names so a hue shift can never reframe a self-report as a judgment.

rules.name: The Scoped-World Rule
rules.body: Every bootcamp palette lives behind a wrapper class with prefixed tokens and never resolves outside it.

rules.name: The No-Serif-In-Drills Rule
rules.body: Serif stays in lessons; drills and the shell are sans-only so a drill reads as a focused workspace.

rules.name: The Layer-Don't-Glow Rule
rules.body: On the dark shell, depth comes from near-black tonal steps and shadow opacity, not neon glow.

rules.name: The Diffuse-Soft-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Light-room shadows are large-radius and very low opacity (<=0.05). Cards float; they do not cast hard 2014-app drop shadows.

dos: Do build new chassis surfaces on the HSL token vocabulary; extend the tokens, don't inline hex.
Do keep color semantic: state tokens for meaning, the bronze ember for rare warmth, nothing chromatic for decoration.
Do scope any new bootcamp world behind its own wrapper class with prefixed tokens.
Do compute the next step and present one CTA, never a grid of equal options.
Do float light-room cards on diffuse low-opacity shadow and convey dark-shell depth through near-black layering.
Do route every progress claim, badge, and CTA to real data.
donts: Don't use border-left/right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe, including via inset box-shadow.
Don't ship gradient text (background-clip: text over a gradient).
Don't spray glassmorphism; the glass blur token is for rare purposeful use.
Don't build the hero-metric template (giant number + tiny label + gradient accent).
Don't add new inline-hex palettes; promote any room identity to named tokens instead of starting a fifth dialect.
Don't import the generic LSAT-prep playbook: card-grid hubs, streak flames, XP bars, or support-desk chat patterns.
Don't animate layout properties except the drill progress bar; animate opacity, transform, color, box-shadow. No bounce, no elastic.
Don't show fabricated telemetry as if it were real progress.
